_meta.title: Plesca Taxonomy of Attack Primitives
_meta.source: From Cipher to Shadow (Plesca, 2024), Chapter 10 and Appendix C
_meta.citation: Plesca, C. S. (2024). From cipher to shadow [Doctoral dissertation]. Chapter 10.
_meta.note: This file contains the high-level taxonomy structure. Full definitions of all 847 attack primitive types are available in the supplementary technical report.

CEA.name: Confidentiality-Exposure Axis
CEA.objective: Obtain information that should not be available to the adversary
CEA.description: Attacks on the CEA aim to breach the boundary between authorized and unauthorized access to information.

AIA.name: Authentication-Impersonation Axis
AIA.objective: Subvert mechanisms by which systems and users verify identity
AIA.description: Attacks on the AIA aim to forge, bypass, or degrade authentication, allowing adversaries to assume false identities.

ICA.name: Integrity-Corruption Axis
ICA.objective: Introduce false information or corrupt existing information
ICA.description: Attacks on the ICA aim to modify data, code, or system state in ways that serve adversarial goals.

Physical.name: TEMPEST / electromagnetic emanation interception
Physical.description: Exploiting electromagnetic emissions from electronic equipment to recover processed data without physical contact.

Physical.name: Acoustic cryptanalysis
Physical.description: Recovering cryptographic keys or processed data from sounds produced by computing equipment during operation.
Physical.primary_defense: Acoustic isolation, randomized computation, sound masking

Physical.name: Cold boot attack
Physical.description: Recovery of encryption keys from DRAM modules after power loss by freezing memory to extend data remanence.
Physical.primary_defense: Full memory encryption, rapid key erasure on power loss, Secure Enclave / TrustZone

Physical.name: Power analysis (SPA/DPA)
Physical.description: Inferring cryptographic secrets from power consumption variations during cryptographic operations.
Physical.primary_defense: Constant-time implementations, power line filtering, balanced logic cells

Physical.name: Optical emanation recovery
Physical.description: Recovering screen content from optical emanations (e.g., LED activity, reflected light from keyboards).

Physical.name: Dumpster diving
Physical.description: Recovery of sensitive information from discarded physical documents or storage media.
Physical.primary_defense: Shredding policies, secure disposal procedures, clear desk policy

Physical.name: Direct physical storage access
Physical.description: Physical theft or unauthorized access to storage devices (laptops, drives, servers).
Physical.primary_defense: Full-disk encryption, remote wipe capability, physical security controls

Logical.name: Network eavesdropping
Logical.description: Passive interception of network traffic to capture plaintext or weakly protected communications.
Logical.primary_defense: End-to-end encryption (TLS 1.3+), VPN

Logical.name: Man-in-the-middle (MITM) interception
Logical.description: Active interposition between communicating parties to intercept and optionally modify communications.
Logical.primary_defense: Certificate pinning, HSTS preloading, mutual TLS

Logical.name: Traffic analysis
Logical.description: Extraction of information from observable communication properties (timing, volume, frequency) without decryption.
Logical.primary_defense: Traffic shaping, padding, mix networks, cover traffic

Logical.name: Timing side-channel attack
Logical.description: Inferring secret values from variations in computation time during cryptographic or security-sensitive operations.
Logical.primary_defense: Constant-time cryptographic implementations

Logical.name: Cache side-channel attack (Spectre/Meltdown class)
Logical.description: Exploiting shared CPU cache state to extract data from processes with higher privilege or different security domains.
Logical.primary_defense: Microarchitectural mitigations, process isolation, site isolation in browsers

Logical.name: SQL injection (data exfiltration)
Logical.description: Injection of malicious SQL to extract unauthorized data from a database.
Logical.primary_defense: Parameterized queries, least-privilege database accounts, WAF

Logical.name: Directory traversal / path injection
Logical.description: Manipulation of file path references to access files outside the intended directory.
Logical.primary_defense: Input validation, path canonicalization, sandboxing

Logical.name: API key / credential exfiltration
Logical.description: Extraction of API keys, tokens, or credentials from code, configuration files, or environment variables.
Logical.primary_defense: Secrets management systems, pre-commit credential scanning, environment isolation

Social.name: Phishing (credential/data harvest)
Social.description: Deceptive electronic communication designed to manipulate recipients into disclosing credentials or sensitive data.
Social.primary_defense: MFA, email filtering, security awareness training

Social.name: Pretexting
Social.description: Impersonation of a trusted party to manipulate an individual into disclosing information.
Social.primary_defense: Callback verification procedures, identity verification protocols

Social.name: Shoulder surfing
Social.description: Direct observation of a user's screen, keyboard, or other input to capture sensitive information.
Social.primary_defense: Privacy screens, clear desk policy, user awareness

Social.name: OSINT aggregation
Social.description: Passive collection and correlation of publicly available information to derive security-sensitive intelligence.
Social.primary_defense: Data minimization, employee privacy awareness, minimal public footprint policy

Combinatorial.name: Hardware supply chain compromise
Combinatorial.description: Compromise of hardware components during manufacturing or distribution to provide covert access or exfiltration capability.
Combinatorial.primary_defense: Trusted hardware supply chain, component verification, hardware attestation

Combinatorial.name: Software supply chain compromise
Combinatorial.description: Compromise of software build systems, dependencies, or distribution infrastructure to inject malicious code at scale.
Combinatorial.primary_defense: SBOM, code signing, reproducible builds, dependency pinning

Combinatorial.name: Advanced persistent threat (APT) exfiltration
Combinatorial.description: Long-term, covert infiltration of high-value targets for systematic intelligence collection.
Combinatorial.primary_defense: Defense in depth, EDR, network behavioral monitoring, threat intelligence

Physical.name: Biometric spoofing
Physical.description: Use of fabricated biometric artifacts (fake fingerprints, face masks, iris prints) to defeat biometric authentication.
Physical.primary_defense: Liveness detection, multi-modal biometrics, continuous authentication

Physical.name: RFID cloning
Physical.description: Cloning of RFID-based access credentials (badge, card, fob) for unauthorized physical access.

Physical.name: Hardware token theft
Physical.description: Physical theft of hardware authentication tokens (FIDO2 keys, OTP generators).

Logical.name: Password brute force
Logical.description: Systematic trial of all possible password combinations until the correct one is found.
Logical.primary_defense: Account lockout, CAPTCHA, MFA, strong password requirements

Logical.name: Dictionary attack
Logical.description: Password attack using precomputed lists of common passwords, words, and variations.
Logical.primary_defense: Salted hashing (Argon2id, bcrypt), MFA, breach credential monitoring

Logical.name: Credential stuffing
Logical.description: Automated use of leaked credential pairs from other breaches to access accounts on target services.
Logical.primary_defense: MFA, breach credential monitoring (HaveIBeenPwned API), bot detection

Logical.name: Session hijacking
Logical.description: Theft or forgery of session tokens to impersonate authenticated users.
Logical.primary_defense: Secure/HttpOnly cookies, session token binding, short session lifetimes

Logical.name: OAuth token abuse
Logical.description: Exploitation of OAuth flows or stolen access tokens to gain unauthorized access to resources.
Logical.primary_defense: Minimal token scopes, short-lived tokens, refresh token rotation

Logical.name: Kerberos ticket forgery (Golden/Silver ticket)
Logical.description: Forgery of Kerberos tickets using compromised KRBTGT key material to impersonate any user in a domain.
Logical.primary_defense: Protected Users security group, Privileged Access Workstations, KRBTGT rotation

Social.name: Help desk impersonation
Social.description: Impersonation of a legitimate user to convince help desk staff to reset credentials or grant access.
Social.primary_defense: Callback verification, manager approval, identity verification protocols

Social.name: SIM swapping
Social.description: Social engineering of mobile carriers to transfer a victim's phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM.
Social.primary_defense: SIM lock / carrier PIN, hardware authentication tokens instead of SMS OTP

Social.name: Business email compromise (BEC) impersonation
Social.description: Impersonation of executives or trusted parties to authorize fraudulent transactions or access.
Social.primary_defense: Out-of-band verification, dual approval for financial transactions

Combinatorial.name: Certificate authority compromise
Combinatorial.description: Compromise of a trusted certificate authority to issue fraudulent certificates for arbitrary domains (DigiNotar 2011 pattern).
Combinatorial.primary_defense: CAA DNS records, Certificate Transparency monitoring, multi-path validation

Combinatorial.name: Authentication hardware seed theft
Combinatorial.description: Theft of cryptographic seed material from hardware token manufacturers (RSA SecurID 2011 pattern).
Combinatorial.primary_defense: Air-gapped seed storage, hardware security modules, post-compromise rotation

Physical.name: Hardware implant (firmware modification)
Physical.description: Physical insertion of malicious hardware or persistent firmware modification to enable covert access or sabotage.
Physical.primary_defense: Firmware attestation, Secure Boot, hardware supply chain security

Physical.name: Physical record modification
Physical.description: Direct physical alteration of paper records, labels, or other physical information artifacts.
Physical.primary_defense: Physical security controls, tamper-evident materials, access logs

Logical.name: SQL injection (data modification)
Logical.description: Injection of malicious SQL to insert, update, or delete database records.
Logical.primary_defense: Parameterized queries, WAF, database integrity constraints, audit logging

Logical.name: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
Logical.description: Injection of malicious scripts into web pages served to other users, enabling content modification and data theft.
Logical.primary_defense: Content Security Policy, output encoding, input validation

Logical.name: DNS poisoning
Logical.description: Corruption of DNS cache entries to redirect DNS queries to attacker-controlled servers.
Logical.primary_defense: DNSSEC, DNS-over-HTTPS/TLS, source port randomization

Logical.name: BGP hijacking
Logical.description: Announcement of false BGP routes to reroute internet traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure.
Logical.primary_defense: RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure), BGPsec, route origin monitoring

Logical.name: Software update mechanism compromise
Logical.description: Compromise of software update infrastructure to distribute malicious updates to large populations.
Logical.primary_defense: Code signing with hardware-protected keys, update integrity verification, staged rollouts

Logical.name: Log tampering
Logical.description: Modification or deletion of audit logs to conceal attacker activity or introduce false records.
Logical.primary_defense: Write-once logs, remote log shipping, cryptographic log integrity (append-only)

Social.name: Deliberate misinformation campaigns
Social.description: Coordinated injection of false information into organizational decision-making processes or public information channels.
Social.primary_defense: Source verification, information provenance tracking, information governance policy

Social.name: Insider data manipulation
Social.description: Intentional corruption of data by an authorized insider for financial, competitive, or ideological gain.
Social.primary_defense: Separation of duties, dual-control for critical data, behavioral monitoring, audit trails

Combinatorial.name: Software supply chain attack (SolarWinds pattern)
Combinatorial.description: Compromise of a widely-deployed software package's build or distribution system to inject malicious code delivered as a legitimate update to thousands of organizations simultaneously.
Combinatorial.primary_defense: SBOM, build integrity attestation, network monitoring for anomalous traffic from trusted software

Combinatorial.name: Cryptographic standard subversion (BULLRUN/Dual_EC pattern)
Combinatorial.description: Introduction of weaknesses into cryptographic standards or reference implementations to create exploitable backdoors in widely-deployed systems.
Combinatorial.primary_defense: Open standards processes, cryptographic agility, diverse independent implementations, formal verification

Combinatorial.name: AI training data poisoning
Combinatorial.description: Corruption of training data or fine-tuning inputs to introduce systematic biases, backdoors, or degraded security properties into machine learning models used in security applications.
Combinatorial.primary_defense: Training data provenance tracking, adversarial robustness testing, data sanitization
